title: THE SEVENTH DAY, THE SEVENTH TIME

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the seventh day, they got up at daybreak and marched around the city seven times in the same manner, except that on that day they circled the city seven times. The seventh time around, when the priests sounded the trumpet blast, Joshua commanded the army, "Shout! For the Lord has given you the city!" — Josh 6:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The seventh day arrives, and this time everything intensifies. They rise at daybreak and march not once but seven times around the city. The number seven runs all through this story — seven priests, seven trumpets, seven days, seven circuits on the seventh day. In Scripture seven often speaks of completeness, of God's perfect fullness. God was doing something whole and complete, in His perfect way and time.

Then comes the long-awaited moment. Joshua cries out, "Shout! For the Lord has given you the city!" Notice again the tense. He does not say, "Shout, and maybe God will give the city." He says, "The Lord HAS given you the city." Even before the walls fall, Joshua speaks with total confidence in God's promise. Faith declares the victory on the strength of God's word, before it can see the result.

There is a lesson here about the boldness of faith. Joshua could shout in confidence because his confidence rested not in the shout but in God's sure promise. Our faith, too, is only as strong as the One in whom it rests — and our God never fails to keep His word.

After all the silence of the previous days, now was the moment to shout. There is a time to wait quietly and a time to declare God's victory boldly. When God says "now," faith responds without hesitation. For us, every victory ultimately rests on what Christ has already accomplished; we shout not to earn the triumph but to celebrate the triumph God has given.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you speak of God's promises with the confidence Joshua had — "the Lord HAS"?
2. Is there a moment where God is now calling you to move boldly after a season of waiting?
3. Does your confidence rest in your own effort, or in God's sure word?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me faith that trusts Your promises before I see the results. Help me wait quietly when I should, and shout boldly when You say "now." Amen.
